stage1.impression: A clean, competent archviz frame of a narrow timber-and-terrazzo bar. It still reads as CG, not as a photograph: surfaces are smooth and evenly lit, the identical stools and slats repeat, there is no atmosphere or sign of life, and the top fifth is an empty black ceiling. The lit band under the ceiling reads as a salmon-pink lightbox, closer to signage than to amber acrylic. No EARF speaker is visible, so the band is the only saturated colour. As it stands a magazine would see a generic, well-proportioned bar rather than a specific, well-made place.

blocking_9: The acrylic band reads as amber cast acrylic with glowing fin edges, not a pink lightbox: delta_e2000 to #FFB347 under 10 and clip_pct under 1 in [300,180,880,245]
Pools of light on the quartzite bar top with dark between them (lum_p95 of the bar top at least 140), and the back-bar bottles catching highlights
The lantern's baffle is no longer the brightest flat plane in the frame: lum_median 55 to 70 with a visible falloff, and the porch is lit as the destination
The ceiling stops reading as a void: less of it in frame, and haze that shows the downlight cones
Materials hold up at 1:1: oak with board-to-board tone variation and no repeated plank texture, terrazzo with readable chips, quartzite with veining and reflections
Signs of life: a record out of its sleeve, glasses with drink and ice, a coat or bag on the banquette, stools not perfectly aligned
A reason to see EARF in the frame: the Tropos glow or Ember tint visible through the porch, or a tinted Core/Hemisphere reading as the one colour accent

defects.what: The acrylic band is salmon-pink (RGB median 248/158/134) with 7.4 % clipping. It reads as a flat lightbox, and the fin edges and reflections are not visible
Empty black ceiling, lum_median 11.9 over 16 % of the frame, with no structure, no haze and no downlight cones
The baffle is the brightest broad plane (median 83), its slats perfectly uniform and evenly lit. It reads as a CG texture
The porch's vertical boards are identical in width and tone and read like a curtain or a laminate, with no oak grain at 1:1
The terrazzo counter face is a dark noise speckle (median 18.9) with no readable chip scale. It reads as carpet
The bar top is evenly dim (median 48, p95 93) with no pools from the five counter spots and no visible veining or reflection
Six identical stools in a perfectly regular row, a repeated model
The oak rail over the banquette shows a repeating plank texture tile
The right wall and the banquette fall into murk (median 20.8). The leather does not read as leather
The pendants read as plain white domes with no tint and add little light to the counter
No props of life (records, coats, filled glasses) and no atmosphere. It reads as a showroom before opening

changes.problem: The band reads as a pink lightbox rather than amber smoked acrylic, and it clips.

change.setting: the lantern's band emission; render white_balance_tint
change.to: emission 0.45 with a 2200 K amber emitter colour; white_balance_tint +1.0

changes.expected: An amber band, not pink, with the fins' polished edges and the gaps between them readable, and no clipping

changes.problem: The counter has no pools of light. The quartzite top is uniformly dim and the back bar's glassware barely sparkles.

change.to: 38.0 W, 18.0 deg, aimed at the centre of the top, with a glass placed under each pool

changes.expected: Five distinct pools on the bar top with darker gaps between them, and highlights on the glasses

changes.problem: The baffle is the brightest broad surface, flatly lit, so the eye stops on a timber wall and not on the lantern's band or porch.

change.to: area 0.35 W/m2, 2400 K, moved to the top edge so it rakes the slats and falls off downward

changes.expected: The slats hold shadow in their reveals, the wall falls off toward the floor, and the band and porch lead

changes.problem: The top 16 % of the frame is an empty black ceiling that adds nothing and makes the room read cavernous instead of cozy.

change.to: lens 32 mm, target [13.0, 4.3, 1.8], camera height kept at 1.45 with verticals kept true (shift, not tilt)

changes.expected: The band sits near the top fifth, the ceiling void halves, and the counter, porch and banquette fill the frame

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere. The downlights and the band light nothing in the air, so the volume reads as CG vacuum.

evidence.measured: ceiling lum_range 17.7, no visible cones under the pendants or spots

changes.expected: Soft cones under the counter spots and a faint glow below the band. The ceiling lifts slightly without flattening

changes.problem: The banquette and right wall sink into murk, so the leather and oak rail do not read.

change.to: 20.0 W, 20.0 deg, one pool per table

changes.expected: The table tops and the leather seat pick up pools, while the wall above stays dark

changes.problem: The oak and the terrazzo read as CG at 1:1: identical boards, a repeating plank tile, and a terrazzo face that is noise.

evidence.measured: porch lum_range 80 with uniform board tones; counter face [0,560,460,800] median 18.9, p95 59, and the chips are not resolvable

change.setting: oak tone per board; terrazzo chip size and ground tone
change.from: a uniform oak tone with a tiled grain; fine chips on a dark ground
change.to: a per-board random tone of plus or minus 8 % and an untiled grain on the porch, baffle and rail; chips 8 to 15 mm on a mid-grey warm ground

changes.expected: The boards differ visibly, there is no repeat on the rail, and the counter face reads as terrazzo with individual chips

changes.problem: Nothing says anyone is here. The stools are a perfect repeated row and the glasses are empty.

evidence.measured: six identical stools at identical spacing and rotation; empty glasses on the counter and tables

change.to: two filled glasses with ice on the bar, a record out of its sleeve leaning at the counter's end, a jacket on the banquette, and the stools rotated and offset by a few degrees and centimetres

changes.expected: A lived-in moment with small highlights in the glasses, so the frame reads as a room at night

out_of_scope.request: Show the Tropos pair (Ember) or another EARF piece in this frame as the colour hero
out_of_scope.why: The products' placement and the porch are fixed. Only the spots inside the lantern may change, and this camera cannot see into it. The owner should decide whether this frame needs a view through the porch.

out_of_scope.request: Read the pendants as tinted Hemispheres/Cores rather than white domes
out_of_scope.why: The product tints are fixed as placed. If these are meant to be tinted, the model, not the light, is wrong.
The furniture as drawn is fixed. Only its placement can be loosened, as in c8.
